formal_statement:
¬ (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (j a b : ℕ) (op : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp),
  (op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨ op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) →
  C.gates[j]? = some { op := op, inputs := [a, b] } →
  a < n + j →
  (∀ x : Fin n → Bool,
      (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD a false = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.eval op [] →
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n
          { gates := C.gates.set j { op := op, inputs := [] }, output := C.output } x =
        PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n C x) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n
      { gates := C.gates.set j { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [a] },
        output := C.output } =
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n C ∧
  (C.gates.set j { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [a] }).length =
    C.gates.length)
plain_statement: It is false that: C is a circuit on n inputs whose gate j is an AND (or an OR) of wires a and b, with a an earlier wire (AND and OR of fan-in two; other gates may be of any operation); other gates may read any wires, and a forward read sees false. Suppose that on every input where wire a is true (for an OR: false), forcing gate j to the constant true (for an OR: false) leaves the circuit's output unchanged. Then replacing gate j by a copy of wire a leaves the function unchanged, and the circuit has as many gates as before.
title: It is false that: Drop rewrite: in a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit, a gate whose second input is a don't-care may become a copy of its first input, same function an
